gumtree_entries.description: UPDATED o2 -> i2: Test.
ADDED i3: Pre-computed PROLEPTIC_MONTH values used in getLong / with test tables. PROLEPTIC_MONTH counts total Pax months elapsed from the epoch, accumulating an extra mo
ADDED i6: --- Pax year 1 start: Pax 0001-01-01 = ISO 0000-12-31 (offset by one day) ---
ADDED i7: --- End of Pax month 1, start of month 2 in year 1 ---
ADDED i8: --- Year 6 is a leap year (last two digits "06" divisible by 6): month 13 is the 7-day Pax month, month 14 is the standard last month ---
ADDED i9: --- Year 399 is a leap year (ends in 99); year 400 is NOT (divisible by 400) ---
ADDED i10: --- Year 0 (BCE 1): non-leap year, standard 13-month structure ---
ADDED i11: --- Historical dates for spot-check ---
ADDED i12: --- Year 2012 is a leap year (ends in 12, divisible by 6) ---
ADDED i13: --- Negative (BCE) years: year -6 is a leap year (abs(-6 % 100) = 6, divisible by 6) ---
ADDED i14: --- Year -99 is a leap year (ends in 99); year -100 is also a leap year (ends in 00, not div by 400) ---
ADDED i15: Invalid: day and month both zero
ADDED i16: Invalid month numbers (out of range for non-leap year)
ADDED i17: Invalid day-of-month for a standard 28-day month
ADDED i18: Year 1900 is a leap year (ends in 00, not divisible by 400): month 13 is the 7-day Pax month; day 8+ is invalid, and month 14 caps at 28
ADDED i19: Year 1898 is NOT a leap year: month 13 is a standard 28-day month, so month 14 doesn't exist at all
ADDED i20: Duplicate coverage for leap-year month 14 boundary (same as 1900 block above)
ADDED i21: Day 29 is invalid in every standard Pax month (months 2–12 have exactly 28 days)
ADDED i22: Year 2001 is not a leap year (364 days), so day 365 is out of range
ADDED i24: Reference implementation mirrors PaxChronology.isLeapYear logic
ADDED i25: 400 is divisible by 400 → NOT a leap year
ADDED i26: 100 ends in 00 and is not divisible by 400 → leap year
ADDED i27: 99 ends in 99 → leap year
ADDED i28: 7 has no qualifying last-two-digits → not a leap year
ADDED i29: 6 ends in 06 (divisible by 6) → leap year
ADDED i30: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 → not leap years
ADDED i31: Negative years: same rule applies to abs(year % 100)
ADDED i32: Year 1900 is a leap year: months 1–12 have 28 days, month 13 (Pax) has 7, month 14 has 28
ADDED i33: Pax (leap) month — only 7 days
ADDED i34: Non-leap years 1901–1905: month 13 is a standard 28-day month
ADDED i35: Year 1906 ends in 06 (divisible by 6) → leap year, month 13 has 7 days
ADDED i36: Year 2000 is divisible by 400 → NOT a leap year, month 13 has 28 days
ADDED i37: Year 2100 ends in 00 but is not divisible by 400 → leap year, month 13 has 7 days
ADDED i39: CE years: proleptic year equals year-of-era directly
ADDED i40: BCE years: proleptic year = 1 - yearOfEra (BCE 1 → proleptic 0, BCE 2 → proleptic -1, …)
ADDED i41: Only PaxEra is accepted; passing an IsoEra must throw ClassCastException
ADDED i44: --- Day-of-month range: 1–28 for standard months, 1–7 for the Pax leap month (13) ---
ADDED i45: Pax leap month: max day is 7
ADDED i46: --- Month-of-year and day-of-year ranges differ between leap and non-leap years ---
ADDED i47: 2012 is a leap year → 14 months
ADDED i48: 2012 is a leap year → 371 days
ADDED i49: --- Aligned-week-of-month: 1–4 for standard months, 1–1 for the 7-day Pax month ---
ADDED i50: Pax month has only 1 week
ADDED i51: --- Non-leap year 2011 comparisons ---
ADDED i52: Month 13 is standard (28 days) in 2011
ADDED i53: 2011 has only 13 months
ADDED i54: 2011 has 364 days
ADDED i55: Standard month → 4 weeks
ADDED i57: All entries use Pax date 2014-05-26 unless noted. Day 26 of month 5 = (4 full months × 28) + 26 = 138th day of year.
ADDED i58: 4 months × 28 + 26 = 138
ADDED i59: day 26 in month = week 4, day 5
ADDED i60: CE
ADDED i61: CE
ADDED i62: BCE
ADDED i64: Format: {srcYear, srcMonth, srcDom, field, value, expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDom}

ADDED i66: non-leap: month 13 has 28 days
ADDED i67: leap: Pax month has 7 days, clamped
ADDED i69: Month 13 in leap year 2012 is the 7-day Pax month; last day is 7
ADDED i73: Format: {srcYear, srcMonth, srcDom, amount, unit, expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDom}
ADDED i74: --- Cross-leap-year arithmetic ---
ADDED i75: leap month 13 + 3 months
ADDED i76: non-leap month 13 → leap month 14
ADDED i77: forward to leap year
ADDED i78: both leap years
ADDED i79: Pax month preserved
ADDED i80: --- Negative (BCE) year arithmetic ---
ADDED i81: Cases where a result lands in the 7-day Pax leap month (day clamped to 7)
ADDED i82: +1 month lands in Pax month; day 26 clamped to 7
ADDED i83: -1 month also lands in Pax month; day clamped
ADDED i84: Pax month to non-leap month 13
ADDED i85: Cases symmetric to data_plus_leap, exercising minus direction
ADDED i86: -(-1) month = +1, bringing day back to 26
ADDED i87: Uses data_plus with reversed parameter binding: the "expected" columns from data_plus become the starting date, and the "source" columns become the expected res
ADDED i89: Format: {year1, month1, dom1, year2, month2, dom2, unit, expected}
ADDED i90: --- Cross-leap-year YEARS arithmetic edge cases ---
ADDED i91: Pax month day 6 in leap vs non-leap year: not a full year apart
ADDED i92: Crossing the Pax month boundary constitutes a full year
ADDED i93: Format: {year1, month1, dom1, year2, month2, dom2, yearPeriod, monthPeriod, dayPeriod}
ADDED i94: --- Cross-leap-year period cases ---
ADDED i96: ISO Period is not compatible with Pax chronology
